| 31 | A check must assert a PROPERTY, never a state the work is expected to change. This session broke the SAME proof EIGHT times, and EVERY failure was because the work SUCCEEDED: QC-10 pinned `task_vscode_app` (then `task` was registered); QC-11 pinned `channel_registry` REFUSED (then the pair was merged); QC-19 pinned `brief_gap > 0` (then the brief was fixed); QC-25 pinned a `row_count` (then registering the word changed it); QC-28 pinned a count of the live gap; QC-31 pinned `version` unmeasurable (then the consistency rule resolved it); QC-32 depended on the live gap being non-empty; QC-40 pinned a live retirements count. | A proof asserts a concrete CURRENT value, so it encodes the DEFECT rather than the RULE. The value moves when the work works, and the check goes red for the wrong reason. | Assert the property (ALL / none / a mechanism on a temp copy). For a mechanism, RE-ACTIVATE the fixed state inside the temp copy so the check measures the MECHANISM, not the live DB. | `python _proof_unified_language.py` | draft |
| 32 | The population you measure must be the population the rule governs. A naming law was enforced against a pool that covered live objects ONLY, so words that appeared ONLY inside a term_key never became candidates: MEASURED, 328 of 2232 active term_keys (14.7%) would be refused if created today. Widening the pool to `all_names` (tables/views UNION active term_keys) moved it 14.7% -> 3.7% with no change to the law. | `real_names` was a convenient population and the law was written against it; a `term_key` is a name the law governs, so the two populations were not the same set. | Name the population in the code (`all_names`) and re-measure the refusal ratio after every rule change. | `python register_vocabulary.py --words --no-classify --limit 900` | draft |
| 33 | A writer that CREATES the thing it then measures pollutes its own measurement. Registering a word writes a row whose `term_key` IS that word, so `used_in` counted the word as a use of ITSELF (endpoint 37 -> 38) and `senses` returned its OWN definition — a role claim then PASSED, i.e. the definition certified itself. | The scan read ALL rows including the one the write had just created, and the exclusion keyed on the TEXT, which the design later changed, so the cycle reopened. | Exclude the subject itself from its own usage, and key the exclusion on a STABLE marker (the cite), not on text. | `python _proof_unified_language.py` | draft |

## Summary

| applicable | measured | PASS | FAIL | UNMEASURED | PROVEN |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 47 | 11 | 7 | 4 | 36 | 0 |

**UNMEASURED is not a pass.** A factor with no proof row has not been measured, and an absent measurement is not a passing one.

**PROVEN requires a STREAK, not a single proof.** A factor with one proof row is MEASURED; it becomes PROVEN only when its `proof_prefix` streak reaches the target. The streak is read from `activation_gate.streak_detail()` — the ONE definition of "streak" — so the generator and the activation gate cannot disagree about the same evidence.
